title: CHRISTMAS IN THE VILLAGE
full_story:
Families and community members are invited to celebrate the holiday season in downtown Louisville on Sunday as “Christmas in the Village” returns with a full schedule of free activities, local food vendors, and festive entertainment.

The event, which runs from 3:00 pm to 8:00 pm, transforms the downtown area around the courthouse and Village Hall into a winter wonderland featuring 28 different activity stops, crafts, and seasonal treats.

The centerpiece of the evening takes place at 6:00 pm with the official tree lighting ceremony and the arrival of Santa and Mrs. Claus.  Visitors can enjoy free horse-drawn carriage rides throughout the event from 3:00 pm to 8:00 pm, with a brief pause around 6:00 pm for Santa’s arrival.  The Full Armor Bell Choir will perform at the Veterans Tree at 4:00 pm and 5:00 pm.  Full Armor FFA students will also present a Live Nativity near Village Hall, alongside a Nativity Festival hosted at Louisville Baptist Church.  Wabash Communications is presenting holiday movie screenings with showtimes at 5:15 pm and 7:00 pm at Diamond Dons Laundry Mat.

Attendees can start at Holiday Headquarters to pick up maps and kids’ goodie bags before exploring dozens of free stations hosted by local businesses and civic groups, Children can enjoy free mini canvas painting at Zink’s Art Studio, face painting at the Old Soda Fountain, sand ornament making at the Clay County Extension, free reindeer games at Clay County State Bank, and make-and-take cookie kits courtesy of the Clay County Farm Bureau.  Mrs. Claus will appear at the Clay County GOP office from 3:00 pm to 5:30 pm, followed by the Grinch from 5:30 pm to 8:00 pm.  Additional character meet-and-greets will take place at Blaine Wilhour’s office and Fat Dad’s, which will feature Frozen characters.  Free s’more kits will be handed out to the first 200 participants at the S’more Station, alongside free kids’ meals at Cruz Restaurant, free Olaf sundaes at Fat Dad’s, and free popcorn, candy, and refreshments scattered across town.  Hungry visitors can also stop by local food trucks including Blaze & Glaze Pizza Co., Blue Bird Baked Goods, Kenzie’s Sweet Shop, KRAZY Snowcone, The Fair Lady, and Pop’s Pit BBQ.

title: DEER HARVEST
full_story:
Hunters in Illinois harvested a preliminary total of 48,475 deer during the first weekend of the 2026 Illinois firearm deer season, November 20th through 22nd.  By comparison, hunters harvested 51,409 deer during the first weekend in 2025 and 54,661 in 2024.

In Clay County hunters harvested 997 deer this year as compared to 988 last year.  Other area counties with higher harvest totals this year include Effingham with 779 compared to 699 last year, Jasper with 799 compared to 787 last year, and Marion County with 1,190 compared to 1,164 last year.  Counties with lower harvest totals include Fayette with 1,223 compared to 1,275 last year, Richland with 491 this year compared to 492 last year, and Wayne County with 1,046, compared to 1,097 last year.

Illinois’ seven-day firearm deer season will conclude December 3rd through 6th.  Youth permits are valid during both segments of the firearm deer season.  Additional deer hunting opportunities in the weeks ahead include; Muzzleloader-only deer season December 11th through 13th.  Late-winter antlerless-only and chronic wasting disease deer seasons in select counties only, December 31st through January 3rd and January 15th through 17th.

Archery deer season continues through January 17th.  Archery deer hunting is closed December 3rd through 6th in counties open for firearm deer season.

Visit the Illinois Department of Natural Resources online for additional information about deer hunting opportunities and regulations.

title: ASSESSMENT CHANGES
full_story:
Clay County Supervisor of Assessments, Kindal Eastin, would like to announce that the 2026 Assessment changes have been published.  Property owners that have assessment changes will receive a Notice of Change of Assessment in the mail.

Taxpayers that have any questions or concerns regarding their assessment, please contact the Assessment Office during this time.  All discrepancies of value must be addressed during the 30 days the Board of Review is in session.  Once tax bills are mailed, it is too late to correct any issues based on opinion of value.

If you disagree with your assessment, even if you did not receive a notice, you may file an appeal with the Board of Review within 30 days of publication.  To inquire about how to file, please contact the assessment office at 618-665-3525 extension 5 for a list of the Board of Review Rules and Procedures.  All required forms must be submitted or postmarked by December 11th, or your complaint will not be heard.  The Board of Review cannot hear complaints regarding taxes, only assessed value.

Property owners that wish to review the full publication list, may do so by purchasing a copy of the November 11th, edition of the Clay County Republican.

title: FREEDOM CAUCUS ON GOVERNOR
full_story:
Governor Pritzker has chosen the interests of his campaign donors over the needs of Illinois families by opting out of the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC) plan, according to the Illinois Freedom Caucus.

The Illinois Freedom Caucus is issuing the following statement:

“Pritzker has made it clear the special interests who donate to liberal campaigns are more important to him than the needs of parents and students.  He not only is blocking families from choosing the education path that is best for their kids; he is even blocking the ability of public-school students to get grants for tutoring.

JB Pritzker knows the FSTC would empower families and destroy the government monopoly on education, and his teacher union overlords can’t have that.

Pritzker says, ‘public education needs more investment than ever’, but yet we continue adding $350 million or more to education spending each year, and we need more?  Maybe the answer isn’t to just keep spending more money.  Maybe accountability and real competition would be what is best for Illinois kids.

Once again, the politically connected insiders in Illinois take the win at regular families’ expense.  But this is the billionaire Pritzker way and his actions, while reprehensible, are sadly completely predictable.”

title: NO EFFECTS REPORTED
full_story:
No effects from the detonation of the nation’s stockpile of lead azide have been reported, according to US Environmental Protection Agency and other government officials.

The blast of nearly 10,000 pounds of lead azide took place promptly at 9 am Wednesday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown about 10 miles across the Mississippi River from Illinois.  TV cameras and other videos posted to social media captured two clouds from the explosions.

Wind patterns were predicted to keep any lead fallout away from Illinois as the plume was expected to travel southwest across parts of Iowa into Missouri.  But as of mid-morning Wednesday, no lead fallout had been reported within that path or anywhere around the Middletown plant, according to EPA air monitors.

At a news conference Tuesday, government officials described the projected lead fallout map as a “worst case scenario” and said they were hopeful a variety of mitigation measures would keep any lead contained to the site of the blast.

Federal officials encouraged people living around the plant to evacuate or shelter in place, warning of possible lead dispersion and powerful explosions that could break windows in the area.  No damage was reported, according to the Associated Press.

In a video statement late Wednesday morning, Major Gen. Eric Shirley, the commanding general of the Army Sustainment Command, said the detonation exceeded expectations and all the lead azide was destroyed.

“I believe absolutely that we reduced as close to zero as is absolutely humanly possible the risk to the health and safety of the people of Middletown and the extended communities throughout Iowa,” Shirley said.

Federal Emergency Management Director Cameron Hamilton said federal teams will continue to conduct testing over the coming days for extra peace of mind.  NASA also deployed several aircraft to circle southeast Iowa to monitor air quality.

The detonation was postponed multiple times as a bipartisan cohort of elected officials from the states wrote letters to the Army seeking more information, and Iowa environmental groups filed an unsuccessful lawsuit to stop the detonation.

title: ISP INCREASING PATROLS
full_story:
The Illinois State Police is increasing patrols and ramping up enforcement efforts in advance of the holiday season.  Earlier this month, the ISP began focusing daily resources on I-57 near Mt. Vernon as part of a construction work zone safety initiative.  During the first week in November, ISP issued more than 650 citations and warnings to drivers, completed more than 80 Motor Carrier Safety Inspections, and placed 17 commercial vehicles traveling through these zones Out of Service.

“To help ensure those traveling through the construction zones and those working in it are safe, ISP is increasing collaboration among numerous ISP work units, including Troop 10 Patrol, the Commercial Vehicle Enforcement Bureau, and Special Operations Group, to get drivers to slow down, follow others at a safe distance, move over, and stop driving when distracted – some of the leading causes of crashes,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly.

This high saturation and visibility approach is aimed at deterring speeding and distracted driving in the area to prevent crashes.  In addition to working with ISP to increase patrols, amplify awareness of the project, and address safety in the work zone, the Illinois Department of Transportation has maintained two lanes in each direction during peak or daytime hours, scheduled some of the more impactful work during off-peak hours, reduced speed limits, and added additional lane markings to help guide traffic.

“In any work zone, the people working behind the cones and barricades want to get home safely to their families and loved ones,” said Illinois Transportation Secretary Gia Biagi.  “We appreciate the partnership with Illinois State Police to help build driver awareness and reinforce safer habits when you are behind the wheel in one of our largest, most active work zones anywhere in the state.  Slowing down, following the signs, and avoiding all distractions can save lives – including your own.”

Last year, 50% of crashes ISP handled in Jefferson County occurred in a work zone.  Construction in the two zones on I-57 near Mt. Vernon will continue until June and October 2027.

With this and many other construction projects throughout the state, drivers should allow plenty of time for travel, reduce speed, avoid tailgating, and pay attention to the road.  Speeding, distracted driving, following too closely, and driving while impaired in work zones are serious offenses, which can result in tragic consequences.

The minimum fine for a first offense of speeding in a work zone is $250.  A second offense results in a suspended driver’s license for 90 days and a $750 fine.  If the violation results in injury to another person, the violator’s driver’s license will be suspended for a mandatory period of anywhere between six months and two years.

When approaching a work zone or vehicle with its emergency lights activated, motorists are reminded that the Move Over Law requires them to slow down and move over.  A person who violates the Move Over Law faces a fine of no less than $250 and no more than $10,000 for a first offense.  If the violation results in injury to another person, the violator’s driver’s license will be revoked.  Additional information about ISP related crashes can be found on the ISP Move Over Crash Map.

title: HUNTERS FEEDING ILLINOIS
full_story:
A popular program returns for its fifth season to help feed neighbors in need.  Hunters Feeding Illinois connects hunters, meat processors, and food pantries to bring lean protein to local residents and families, providing a unique pathway to address and improve food insecurity.

In partnership with Feeding Illinois, Access Illinois Outdoors, Southern Illinois Food Pantry Network, and University of Illinois Extension, the program allows hunters to donate harvested deer to partnering meat processors who turn it into ground meat.  Food pantries receive ground venison to share with their guests.

“Food insecurity affects about one in eight Illinois residents, and the challenge is even greater across much of our program area,” said Michelle Fombelle, food and health systems educator.  “With the rising cost of protein, Hunters Feeding Illinois helps ensure families can put nutritious meals on the table while making their food dollars go further.”

Like previous years, hunters can donate whole harvested deer at no cost.  Because processing volume increases throughout the season, hunters are encouraged to call processors in advance to confirm they have slots to accept deer.  Processors have a select number of slots for donated deer, which become more limited as the season continues.

Partnering processors in our area for the hunting season include Blair’s Slaughtering and Processing, and Salt and Strings butchery both in Louisville.

Thanks to our collaboration with Feeding Illinois, donations are doubled dollar for dollar.  A $50 donation becomes $100, which covers the processing of one deer.  Donate online at go.illinois.edu/deerdonation.

During the 2025-2026 hunting season, Hunters Feeding Illinois distributed 40,712 pounds of ground venison to 43 food pantries across east-central and southern Illinois.

To learn more, connect on Facebook, join the email list, or email [email protected].  Visit the website at go.illinois.edu/deerdonation for recipes, videos, and more program information.

title: FRAUDULENT WEBSITES SHUTDOWN
full_story:
Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias announced that his office successfully shut down 51 fraudulent investment websites linked to more than $7.1 million in reported investor losses nationwide as part of an aggressive enforcement effort to combat sophisticated online investment scams.

The announcement came during International Fraud Awareness Week and highlights the Secretary of State’s Securities Department’s efforts to identify, investigate and shut down fraudulent online investment platforms before they can defraud more unsuspecting investors.

As part of a coordinated effort among state securities regulators, the department analyzed 297 websites and successfully shut down 51.  The 51 websites were associated with more than $7.1 million in reported investor losses, according to information reported to the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

“Scammers are getting more sophisticated, more convincing and harder to detect than ever.  Our Securities Department is actively hunting down fraudulent investment websites and working to shut them down before they can victimize more Illinoisans,” Giannoulias said.  “During Fraud Awareness Week, we’re reminding investors to verify that an investment opportunity is legitimate before handing over their hard-earned money.  Do your homework, protect your money and report suspected scams, because one report can help prevent someone else from becoming the next victim.”

The fraudulent websites identified by the department promoted schemes involving cryptocurrency, artificial intelligence-powered trading platforms and other bogus investment opportunities.  Some used tactics associated with romance scams, in which scammers establish personal or romantic relationships with potential victims and gradually convince them to invest increasing amounts of money.

The Securities Department launched its initiative to identify and take down fraudulent investment websites in 2025.  The department works with domain registrars and hosting companies to shut down fraudulent websites and disrupt scammers’ ability to use them to target additional victims.

title: FOOD INFRASTRUCTURE GRANT PROGRAM
full_story:
The Illinois Stewardship Alliance is encouraging farmers, food businesses, cooperatives and eligible community organizations across Illinois to start registration now if they plan to apply for the Fiscal Year 2027 Local Food Infrastructure Grant (LFIG) program.  The Illinois Department of Agriculture will make $1.8 million available for projects that strengthen the state’s local food system.

Applications are now open and must be submitted by noon on January 6th.  Required registrations can take two to four weeks, so applicants who wait until after the holidays to get started risk missing the deadline.

The new funding follows nearly $4 million in grants announced earlier this year to support infrastructure improvements across Illinois, from refrigerated transportation and meat processing equipment to commercial kitchens, food storage facilities and distribution systems.

“Local food doesn’t move itself,” said Liz Moran Stelk, Executive Director of the Illinois Stewardship Alliance.  “A farmer can grow the food and have a customer ready to buy it, and still lose the sale because there’s no affordable way to keep it cold or get it there.  That’s why farmers in our alliance pushed for these grants.”

“We know that 95% of the food we eat in Illinois comes from out of state.  As agriculturally rich and productive as Illinois is, we can change that.  Farmers are ready to meet growing demand for locally produced food, but they need the infrastructure to make that possible.  This new round of funding is an opportunity to strengthen farms, create economic opportunities and help more Illinois-grown food reach Illinois families.”

The program addresses a persistent challenge facing small and mid-sized agricultural producers: the lack of affordable infrastructure connecting farms with local markets.

Individual grants ranging from $1,000 to $75,000 and collaborative grants ranging from $1,000 to $250,000 are available to support qualifying infrastructure projects.

The latest awards demonstrate how those investments can benefit different agricultural businesses and communities.

The Alliance said the program is especially important for smaller producers and food businesses that may lack the resources to make major infrastructure investments independently.

The Alliance said continued interest in LFIG also reinforces the importance of sustained state support for local food infrastructure.  Previous application rounds have generated requests substantially exceeding available funding, demonstrating that infrastructure remains a significant barrier for Illinois producers.
